stories.title: Global Carbon Budget shows projected fossil emissions easing, while overall CO2 rises
stories.summary: A Global Carbon Project assessment presented during COP31 projected global fossil CO2 emissions would dip about 0.4% in 2026 to 38.2 billion metric tonnes. A war-driven increase in oil prices and clean-energy growth contributed, but higher emissions from deforestation and land use could raise total human CO2 output to around 43.3 billion tonnes. Scientists warned that a small forecast annual decline is not evidence of a permanent peak.
stories.whyItMatters: Long-run emissions drive global heating and climate damage; COP31 decisions on energy and forests will matter far more than a temporary reduction in fuel use.
stories.selectionRationale: A globally consequential quantitative scientific release, timed to COP31 and reported independently in three newsrooms. Kept the established COP31 event ID.
stories.evidenceNote: Three original free publisher reports on the same international scientific assessment: Reuters by Sarah McFarlane, Guardian by Fiona Harvey in Antalya, Euronews by Angela Symons. Their newsroom independence does not make their shared underlying data three independent studies.
